- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to prevent overreaction.  
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon (e.g., >0.2 after 10–15 days), model lags in upward correction; add 0.5–1.5% incremental lift to forecast from day 15 onward.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving avg, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence; if below, add 1–2% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true volatility in high-sentiment periods; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment >0.2 for 3+ consecutive days.
